claims.claim: OpenRouter's default provider load-balancer weights selection by the inverse square of price (r=2), documented in OpenRouter's own routing docs.
An X.com long-form article by Tarun Chitra fits an empirical decisiveness parameter r ≈ 1.968 (95% CI 1.82-2.11) from 1,648 observed provider-selection events across 6 models and 35 providers.
Bloomberg reported Stripe finalized an agreement to acquire OpenRouter for more than $7 billion, three months after OpenRouter's $1.3B Series B.
WSJ reported Stripe-OpenRouter acquisition talks around 2026-07-24 at approximately $10 billion, roughly 30% higher than the final ~$7B figure reported three weeks later.
OpenRouter's $113M Series B (2026-05-28), led by CapitalG with NVentures participating, valued the company at approximately $1.3B post-money.

The Information's single-sourced 2026-07-29 exclusive reported OpenRouter's annualized revenue at approximately $140M, implying a ~70x multiple on the then-discussed $10B price; no independent second outlet has corroborated the $140M figure with its own reporting.
Anthropic prices Claude prompt-cache reads at 0.1x base input token price, and cache writes at 1.25x (5-min TTL) or 2x (1-hour TTL).
DeepSeek's context caching discounts cache-hit tokens roughly 10x versus cache-miss tokens, requiring an exact prefix match from token 0.

OpenRouter's own documentation concedes that across its 70+ backend providers, a cache lives only where it was written, so a follow-up turn landing on a different provider instance pays full price with no fraud required — a routing-architecture limit, not necessarily deliberate misreporting.

An academic audit of prompt caching in LLM APIs found that outside auditors have no visibility into provider-internal caching and must infer cache behavior via timing side-channels, detecting caching in 8 of 17 tested providers this way.

Tullock's 1980 contest-success function models win probability as effort^r divided by the sum of all efforts^r; Baye, Kovenock and de Vries (1994) show a symmetric mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium with full rent dissipation exists specifically for r>2, making r=2 the model's structural knife-edge.

Academic literature applying Tullock-contest theory to real infrastructure (blockchain block-building, procurement auctions) proves standard Tullock contests are Sybil-proof — splitting one bid into sub-identities yields no higher payoff than one consolidated bid — the opposite of a claimed multi-entry vulnerability.
StreamLake is a cloud/AI brand created and operated by Kuaishou Technology, not an independently owned company, per corroborating 2022 reporting from Caixin and China Daily on its launch.

Wafer (wafer.ai), which the original article groups with Cerebras as a hardware 'Specialist' charging a premium, describes itself as a software inference-optimization layer running on commodity NVIDIA/AMD/cloud GPUs and raised only an $800K seed round — inconsistent with owning proprietary chip hardware.

Cerebras genuinely serves gpt-oss-120B at roughly 3,000 tokens/second versus roughly 56 tokens/second for the same-class model on Anthropic's own serving, a real ~55x hardware-driven speed differential.

Novita AI's specific figures cited in the critique (repriced roughly 500 times in July; quoting 5-10% of model-builder list price) could not be independently corroborated by any source outside the original article itself; third-party trackers give inconsistent, low-quality data on Novita's basic corporate facts.

OpenRouter's own rankings page explicitly disclaims that its data represents 'the whole market' and shows only rank/raw token counts for its top app, Hermes Agent, never a percentage of platform-wide traffic.

Robot Ventures (co-founded by Tarun Chitra) is confirmed by TechCrunch as both a prior investor in, and the lead of a new $75M round valuing at $1.5B, Nous Research — maker of Hermes Agent, which Chitra's critique names favorably as OpenRouter's largest app.

Paradigm's 2020 'Ethereum is a Dark Forest' essay's core mechanism is the generalized frontrunner: a bot that scans a shared, transparent, pre-settlement mempool for profitable pending transactions and copies them — a structural precondition (public pending state) that has no analogue in OpenRouter's private request/response billing.

Flashbots' own documentation describes MEV-Boost/Proposer-Builder Separation as redistributing who captures MEV via a competitive builder auction, not eliminating extraction — a redistribution fix, not an extraction-elimination fix, weakening its use as precedent for 'fixing' a billing-verification gap.

Edelman, Ostrovsky and Schwarz's foundational 2007 ad-auction paper establishes generalized-second-price equilibrium properties, not a finding about advertiser or platform gaming/misrepresentation as cited.
U.S. v. Google LLC (2023/2025) centered on monopolization and illegal tying of the publisher ad-server and ad-exchange markets; ad-quality misrepresentation was not a pleaded theory in the case.

'Spoofing' under the Commodity Exchange Act (7 U.S.C. § 6c(a)(5)(C)) is a narrow, scienter-requiring doctrine governing regulated futures/derivatives order books, with no jurisdictional hook over a private SaaS marketplace's billing terms.

Gabaix and Laibson's 2006 'shrouded attributes' model shows firms can profitably hide costly attributes from consumers even in fully competitive markets — a closer theoretical fit than antitrust or spoofing law for a headline price that obscures true billed cost.

NVIDIA's H100/H200/Blackwell confidential-computing attestation verifies GPU hardware identity, firmware, and model/runtime integrity — it makes no assertion about workload-level metrics such as KV-cache hit counts or tokens billed.

A 2026 confidential-GPU-inference benchmark under Intel TDX found substantially higher real-world overhead than earlier 2024 studies — up to 21.8-27.8% time-to-first-token increase and 17.7-21.1% throughput loss under load — versus below-7% overhead reported in a 2024 study, showing overhead is highly configuration-dependent.

Zero-knowledge 'verifiable inference' (zkLLM), a lighter-weight cryptographic alternative to full TEE attestation, remains computationally impractical at LLM scale, requiring roughly 800-1,000 seconds to generate and validate a single proof for a 13B-parameter model.

No production confidential-computing deployment attests to cache-hit counts specifically; the one real production GPU-TEE deployment on OpenRouter's marketplace (Phala, serving DeepSeek R1 since February 2025) attests to hardware and model integrity only, not billing reconciliation.

In March 2025, Gauntlet proposed a Compound-Morpho vault arrangement and was itself the largest voter approving its own proposal; The Block's reporting explicitly ties the episode to Robot Ventures (Chitra's fund, co-founded with Compound founder Robert Leshner) holding a stake in Morpho, the party favored by the proposal.

In September 2025, Compound DAO governance faced public backlash over renewing Gauntlet's $2.3M risk-management contract, with critics — including Aave delegate Marc Zeller — explicitly citing conflicts of interest.
Gauntlet terminated its four-year, $1.6M Aave risk-steward relationship in February 2024 amid community criticism, then joined rival protocol Morpho as a risk curator days later.

Unlike a16z, which publishes a standing disclosure that it 'is acting in its own financial interest, not necessarily in the interests of other token holders,' Gauntlet has no discoverable public conflict-of-interest disclosure policy.
Tarun Chitra is founder and CEO of Gauntlet (founded 2018, closed a $125M Series C from SBI Holdings in June 2026) and co-founder/partner of Robot Ventures alongside Compound founder Robert Leshner.
Stripe's relationship with OpenRouter began as a payments vendor (invoicing, tax, fraud detection via Radar) in January 2026, seven months before acquisition talks were reported.

OpenRouter's own Series B announcement reports weekly token volume grew from 5 trillion to 25 trillion tokens over six months, on pace to process over a quadrillion tokens in 2026, serving 8M+ developers across 400+ models.

Sacra's research identifies OpenRouter's routing-margin durability risks as provider concentration, low barriers to entry enabling commoditization, self-hosted alternatives like LiteLLM, and hyperscaler bundling (AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex, Azure OpenAI).

A July 2026 independent researcher post argues OpenRouter cannot guarantee that a request billed against a named model is actually served at the claimed quantization/quality, calling its automated 'Auto Exacto' quality check insufficient for reliable verification — a distinct but adjacent serving-fidelity gap from the cache-billing allegation.

No public response addressing cache-manipulation allegations was found from OpenRouter, Novita, or StreamLake, and no Hacker News or press pickup of the specific 'Caching Cheaters on OpenRouter' claims was found as of 2026-08-19, two days after publication.
